note: Measured on past data. Past behaviour does not mean it will repeat. Costs assume $3.74 per MES round trip (commission plus one tick of slippage each side).

items.title: Overnight vs daytime (S&P 500, since 1993)
items.value: +7.7% a year overnight vs -2.0% a year in the daytime
items.detail: Holding SPY only from the close to the next open earned about 7.7% a year after costs; holding only from the open to the close lost about 2.0% a year. Buy-and-hold earned about 11.4% a year.

items.title: Overnight with the 200-day filter
items.detail: Holding overnight only when the close is above its 200-day average gave up a little return but cut the worst peak-to-trough fall to about 14%. This is the rule the system is now testing on a simulation account.

items.title: MES overnight vs daytime, last two years
items.value: +1.32 and +3.60 points a night; daytime +1.65 and -0.39
items.detail: Average MES move from the 16:00 ET close to the 09:30 ET open, up on 57% of nights in both years, compared with the average move from the open to the close.

items.title: Opening-range breaks often fail
items.detail: The first time price broke out of the 09:30-09:45 ET range, it was back inside that range within 15 minutes on 78% of days.

items.title: The system's earlier daytime setups
items.detail: Replayed over a year of 1-minute data, all six daytime setups the system started with were negative after costs (for example MESRunner lost $3.97 a trade over 161 trades). They are not being used.
